messages:
maya: FYI opened a tiny PR to toggle an example that shows schema-validated tool calls vs permissive parsing. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/958 :eyes:
sam: Can you paste the JS/TS snippet inline? We should add a small migration note for teams that call invokeTool directly.
maya: JS snippet:
```
const resp = await sdk.invokeTool('summarize', prompt);
// safe parse
if (!resp || resp.payload == null) return { status: 'no_content' };
// otherwise handle resp.payload
```
Also added a TS variant using `@redwood/inference` and a short note about package renames.
oliver: Docs CI flagged a broken anchor in the guardrails page and a failing doctest for the Python snippet. Error: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'` when payload is null.
maya: Fixed the anchor and updated the Python helper to be defensive: `payload = response.get('payload') if response else None`. Added a doctest that asserts minimal envelope returned.
docs-bot: Heads up: staging deploy window in ~30m; merging before that will pick this up.
ci-bot: PR #958 checks: docs-tests failed -> now passing after fixes.
sam: tiny wording nit: change "strict schema enforcement" to "validate and fallback" in the guardrails intro so we don't scare customers. Also add a short example for returning a minimal envelope on parse failure.
maya: Done. Added `parse_or_minimal(response, schema)` example and a one-line migration blurb under "v2 structured outputs". Left a TODO to add unit tests for the TS examples.
oliver: Approving now; will merge once CI remains green. Thanks folks! :rocket:
